Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of sourcing and fetching sources. The top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments and array definitions — no command substitution, no `curl`/`wget`/`eval`, and no obfuscated payloads that would execute during sourcing.

The `source` array contains a single entry fetching the package's own upstream tarball from its GitHub repository over HTTPS (`https://github.com/Psysonic/psysonic/archive/refs/tags/app-v$pkgver.tar.gz`). This is exactly the kind of standard source declaration expected for an AUR package. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is explicitly called out in the gate instructions as not grounds for failure on its own — it does not execute code and the SKIP is normal for upstream tarballs at this audit stage.

There is no `pkgver()` function, so no VCS probe logic runs during sourcing. The `build()` and `package()` functions contain standard packaging operations (`npm install`, `npm run tauri:build`, `install` commands, a simple wrapper script via `/dev/stdin` heredoc) that do not execute under `--nobuild --noprepare` and are out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard Tauri-based AUR PKGBUILD, safe for sourcing and source fetch.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Standard Tauri-based AUR PKGBUILD, safe for sourcing and source fetch.

<details>
This is a standard AUR .SRCINFO metadata file for the psysonic package. It declares package metadata (name, version, description, license, dependencies) and a source URL pointing to the official GitHub repository's tagged release tarball (app-v1.52.0). The sha256sums=SKIP is ordinary practice for VCS or mutable sources, though a pinned checksum would be better hygiene. No executable code, network exfiltration, obfuscation, or supply-chain attack indicators are present.

<evidence>

[1/2] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR metadata file, no malicious content.
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices. It builds the psysonic desktop music player from the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/Psysonic/psysonic) using npm and Rust/Tauri toolchains. The build process is straightforward: it sets environment variables for Cargo and npm caches, adjusts linker flags for compatibility with Arch's toolchain, and runs the upstream build commands. The package() function installs the binary, a thin wrapper script at /usr/bin/psysonic that simply execs the binary with arguments, a standard XDG desktop entry, and hicolor icons.

There are no suspicious elements: no obfuscated code, no unexpected network downloads, no eval/base64/curl/wget usage in dangerous contexts, no exfiltration of system files, and no modifications to unrelated system files. The checksum is SKIP, which is normal and expected for AUR packages (especially with tarball sources that may change). The source URL points directly to the package's own declared upstream repository. All dependencies, makedepends, and optdepends are consistent with a Tauri-based desktop application using GStreamer for internet radio playback.

The wrapper script is a simple exec call with proper variable escaping, the desktop entry is a standard XDG specification file, and the icon installations follow the Freedesktop icon theme specification layout. There is no evidence of injected malicious code or supply-chain tampering.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard PKGBUILD building from official upstream source; no malicious behavior detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>
